paper.title_en: Can matter–geometry coupling reduce exotic matter? LQG wormholes in \(f(R,T)\) gravity
paper.abstract_en: We investigate traversable Lorentzian wormhole solutions sourced by the Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG) effective energy density of the Modesto self-dual black hole, embedded in <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1615"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>β</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> modified gravity. Two complementary configurations are examined: the zero-tidal redshift <math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1644"><mrow><mi>Φ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">const</mi></mrow></math> with the shape function derived self-consistently from the field equations (Case A), and the power-law shape function <math altimg="si397.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1654"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> with the redshift function obtained by numerical integration of the resulting Riccati equation (Case B). For Case A a closed-form shape function is obtained, characterised by two structure constants encoding the <math altimg="si319.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1684"><mi>β</mi></math>-dependence, while Case B requires numerical treatment. In both configurations the effective null energy condition combinations acquire a universal multiplicative prefactor <math altimg="si321.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1689"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>β</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> relative to their general relativity counterparts, so that the effective NEC-violating contribution measured by the volume integral quantifier scales as <math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1707"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.16667em"/><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">GR</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>. Where the negative-<math altimg="si319.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1748"><mi>β</mi></math> branch is horizon-free, this coupling suppresses the magnitude of the effective NEC violation; in the prescribed power-law configuration, however, horizon avoidance restricts the viable solutions to <math altimg="si407.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1754"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, for which the explicit rescaling factor exceeds unity; this configuration admits no <math altimg="si254.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1764"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> member and therefore no general-relativistic reference solution. The wormhole geometry conditions, energy conditions, Ricci scalar, and modified Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equilibrium are examined in detail for both cases. Case A recovers the wormhole solutions of Cruz, Neves and Muniz (2024) in the limit <math altimg="si10.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1774"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>; Case B is an independent configuration for which <math altimg="si11.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1784"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is required by the field equations.
